AuditEntryOut.description: One audit row, as the organization may read it. Values never leave the service.
AuditEntryOut.title: AuditEntryOut

CheckoutConfirmIn.description:
`POST /payment/checkouts/{charge_id}/confirm` (Razorpay) — the three fields Checkout's
callback hands the browser. **Proof of nothing**: the server checks the signature as a
precondition, then asks Razorpay what happened. Missing or blank fields are a 400.
CheckoutConfirmIn.title: CheckoutConfirmIn

CheckoutCustomerIn.description:
Who is paying, as the provider's checkout needs it (Cashfree requires a phone on every
Order). **Passed through to the provider and nowhere else** — never stored, logged, audited or
put in an event. A phone is 10 digits, or `+` and 8-15 digits.
CheckoutCustomerIn.title: CheckoutCustomerIn

CollectionWiresOut.description:
Per provider, whether a merchant's adapter talks to the provider for real (`live`) or runs
on the in-process stub (`stub`: a checkout cannot be paid for real).
CollectionWiresOut.title: CollectionWiresOut

MerchantAccountIn.description:
`PUT /payment/collections/merchant-account` — connect the organization's payment-provider
account, or rotate its credentials in place (same provider and mode only: switching is
disconnect, then connect). Needs a session that signed in with a one-time code.

* **Razorpay**: `key_id` (`rzp_test_…` / `rzp_live_…`, public — Checkout is opened with it; the
  mode is read from it, so `mode` is not sent), `key_secret`, `webhook_secret` (the one set on
  the webhook in Razorpay's dashboard).
* **Cashfree**: `key_id` is the App ID, `key_secret` the Secret Key (it also signs webhooks, so
  there is no `webhook_secret`), and `mode` is `sandbox` or `production` — an App ID does not
  say which.
* **PhonePe** (Standard Checkout V2): `key_id` is the Client ID, `key_secret` the Client
  Secret, `webhook_secret` the webhook **password** set in PhonePe's dashboard, `mode`
  `sandbox` or `production`, and `config` exactly `{"client_version": <number>,
  "webhook_username": "<the webhook username>"}`.
* **PayU** (Hosted Checkout): `key_id` is the merchant key, `key_secret` the salt (it also
  verifies webhooks, so there is no `webhook_secret`), and `mode` `sandbox` or `production`.

Secrets are sealed on arrival and never returned — only a masked hint of each.
MerchantAccountIn.title: MerchantAccountIn

MerchantAccountOut.description:
The organization's payment-provider connection as an admin may see it: masked secrets
only, the webhook URL to register at the provider (`?account=` names this account), whether
the credentials have been verified, and when a webhook last arrived.
MerchantAccountOut.title: MerchantAccountOut

PlatformCheckoutIn.description: `POST /payment/checkouts` — open (or reopen) the checkout for one invoice.
PlatformCheckoutIn.title: PlatformCheckoutIn

PlatformCheckoutOut.description:
What the browser needs to open the provider's checkout, and what it will charge.
`amount_minor` and `currency` are the invoice's own charge's. `client_action` is provider-shaped
and tagged by `type`: `{"type": "razorpay_checkout", "key_id", "order_id", "openable"}` (the
**public** key id and the Order id — never the secret) or `{"type": "cashfree_checkout",
"payment_session_id", "mode", "openable"}`. `openable` is False on a stub provider: the Order
is a local stand-in no real checkout would accept. The session token is never stored;
reopening fetches it again. `test_mode` is true when the provider that owns the charge runs on
test / sandbox credentials (a Razorpay `rzp_test_` key on a live wire, or Cashfree's sandbox):
the checkout takes the provider's test cards and no real money moves. False on live
credentials and on a stub.
PlatformCheckoutOut.title: PlatformCheckoutOut

PlatformCheckoutStatusOut.description:
The state of one checkout, as the server knows it. `paid` is true only for a **captured**
payment — one the provider reported, by a status check or a signed webhook; never because a
browser said so. `provider_checked` is false when the provider could not be asked this time
(the state shown is then the last one recorded). A failed checkout with `failure_reason`
`checkout_expired` is one nobody paid before it expired. `test_mode` is as on
`PlatformCheckoutOut`: the owning provider runs on test / sandbox credentials, so `paid` means
paid with a test instrument.
PlatformCheckoutStatusOut.title: PlatformCheckoutStatusOut

ReconciliationOut.description:
A read-only comparison of this platform's collection records with the provider's. It
corrects nothing: a mismatch is for a person to look at (a status check, or the provider's
own dashboard, is what settles it).
ReconciliationOut.title: ReconciliationOut

WebhookAck.description:
The result of ingesting a provider webhook.

`duplicate` is true when the `provider_event_id` was already in the inbox — the callback was a
re-delivery and did nothing the first time did not already do. `reconciled` is true when the
event moved a charge to a terminal state and emitted a `commerce.payment.*`.

`provider_event_id` is the id the inbox deduplicated on: the delivery's `X-Razorpay-Event-Id`
header, else an id the body carried, else `derived:<sha256>` from the body's event name, entity
id and timestamp. It is never empty.

`ignored_reason` is set when the webhook was authentic but cannot be reconciled and never will
be — the provider is answered 200 (a retry could not change the outcome) and the reason is a
stable code: `unknown_charge` and `unattributable` (nothing here to reconcile), or
`illegal_transition`, `amount_mismatch`, `currency_mismatch` and `provider_id_conflict` (it
contradicts what this platform holds; no state was changed, an operator should look). Every
reason except `unattributable` — which has no tenant to record under — is kept on the inbox
row and audited as `payment.webhook.ignored`. Null on a webhook that was reconciled or was
simply a redelivery.
WebhookAck.title: WebhookAck

info.description: The provider-facing edge of commerce: mandates, charges, refunds and the webhook inbox. Razorpay-first, with the provider seam isolated so no other service knows which processor took the money — only that a charge was captured or failed. A failed charge is what suspends a subscription and, in turn, de-entitles a product (ADR-0004 §5).
info.title: Payment service

422.description: A bad cursor, filter or date range

get.summary: The organization's audit trail recorded by this service, newest first

post.description:
Open the provider's hosted checkout for one invoice. The amount is the invoice's own
charge's, never the body's; a second request for an invoice with an open checkout returns that
checkout (at the provider it was created under). **404** if the organization has no charge for
the invoice, **409** if it is already paid (`invoice_already_paid`) or cannot be opened right
now (each with its own code), **422** for what could never be paid online.

The Order handed back is always the one the charge **records**: it is recorded before this
answers, a reopen fetches it by its id, and an Order the call made that the charge does not
record is never handed out (a 409 `checkout_in_progress` instead; the next request gets the
recorded one).

404.description: The organization has no payable charge for this invoice.

409.description: Refused, with a stable machine code in `errors[0].code`: `invoice_already_paid` (field `invoice_id`; the invoice is paid — the only 409 that means paid), `checkout_in_progress` (another request holds the checkout; try again in a moment), `previous_checkout_not_closable` (the expired checkout could not be closed yet; try again shortly), `previous_checkout_payment_in_flight` (a payment on a previous checkout is still being processed; try again in a few minutes), `checkout_not_supported` (the provider has no hosted checkout).

422.description: Could never be paid online, refused before any provider call, with `errors[0] = {field, code, message}`: `phone_required` (field `customer.phone`), `customer_details_required` (field `customer`), `currency_unsupported`, `amount_below_minimum` and `nothing_to_pay` (field `invoice_id`). A malformed body is a 422 with the framework's own field errors.

post.summary: Open (or reopen) the checkout for an invoice

get.description:
Read-through status: while the checkout is open the provider is asked, server to server, what
happened to its Order, and the answer reconciled like a signed webhook's. What the return page
polls. `paid` is true only for a captured payment. A checkout closed as `checkout_expired` is
still asked about inside its late-capture window: a payment made on its Order after it closed is
recorded, and the answer is `paid: true`.
get.summary: The state of one checkout (asks the provider while it is open)

post.description:
Razorpay's Checkout hands the browser `{payment_id, order_id, signature}`. This checks the
signature — `HMAC-SHA256(order_id|payment_id)` under the key secret, in constant time — and that
the Order is this checkout's; a missing field, a mismatch or a signature that is not the digest
is a **400 and nothing is marked paid**. Only then does it ask Razorpay (`order_payments`) and
reconcile the answer. The callback proves nothing: `paid` is true only if that answer shows a
captured payment.
post.summary: Razorpay: verify Checkout's callback signature, then ask Razorpay what happened

delete.description:
Refused (409 `disconnect-blocked`, saying what is outstanding) while the provider may still
move money for the account — an open payment, a cancelled or expired one its provider can
still take, a pending refund — unless `force` is set.

parameters.description: Disconnect even though payments or refunds on the account have not settled. Audited with what was outstanding.
parameters.name: force

schema.description: Disconnect even though payments or refunds on the account have not settled. Audited with what was outstanding.
schema.title: Force

put.description:
Database only: the credentials are checked for shape and sealed, and the account is
`unverified` until `POST …/merchant-account/verify` asks the provider.
put.summary: Connect the organization's Razorpay or Cashfree account, or rotate its credentials

post.description:
Claim (open the key secret, in a short transaction), probe (one authenticated, read-only
request to the provider, with no transaction open, within `collections_call_timeout_seconds`),
record (`verified_at` or `last_error_code`, re-checked under the row lock, audited). A provider
that refuses the credentials is recorded and then answered 422 `credentials-rejected`; one
that cannot be reached records nothing and is a 503.
post.summary: Ask the provider whether the connected account's credentials work

get.description:
Asks the provider, server to server, about the most recent collections and lists every
disagreement. **Corrects nothing** — a status check from the order, or the provider's own
dashboard, is what settles a mismatch.
get.summary: Compare recent online payments with the provider's records (read-only)

get.description:
The service, the provider new checkouts go to and what it runs on: `mode` is `test` when that
provider is on test / sandbox credentials (a staging box under `PAYMENT_ALLOW_TEST_KEYS`).
Names and modes only — never a key or any part of one.

post.description:
Ingest one Cashfree PG webhook. The body is read raw — the signature is
`base64(HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + body))` over exactly these bytes and the
`x-webhook-timestamp` header — and capped before it is touched. A missing secret, header or
match is a 400 with nothing recorded (fail closed).
post.summary: Cashfree webhook — signature-verified, idempotent, reconciling (404 unless enabled)

post.description:
One merchant's webhook, from whichever provider **the account row** names (Razorpay or
Cashfree) — never from this path or the body. The body is read raw — the signature is over
exactly these bytes. An unknown or removed account, a bad signature and an unparseable
account id all answer the same 400, so a prober learns nothing about which accounts exist.
post.summary: A tenant's payment-provider webhook — per-merchant signature, idempotent, reconciling

post.description:
Ingest one Razorpay webhook. The body is read raw — the signature is over exactly these
bytes, so it must not be re-serialized before verification.

Kept forever: every Razorpay merchant registered this path. The same handler as
`/webhooks/collections`; the provider is the account row's, so a delivery here for a Cashfree
account is verified as Cashfree's.
post.summary: The original path of a tenant's webhook — an alias of /webhooks/collections

get.description:
How far behind the relay is. **Alert on `oldest_seconds`.**

A stalled relay is the platform's quietest failure. It selects, finds nothing,
logs nothing, sleeps, and loops — `attempts` never increments and `last_error`
stays null, so the process looks healthy indefinitely while the outbox grows
without bound and every consumer downstream starves.

Deliberately **not** part of readiness. A backlog is not a reason to take the
service out of rotation: refusing traffic would stop new events being written
without helping drain the ones already queued, which makes the incident worse.
This is a metric to alert on, not a health state.

Counted through the outbox engine, not the application one. The app role is
NOBYPASSRLS and this request binds no tenant, so through it `pending` would be
zero whatever the table holds — the probe that exists to expose the stall would
be wired to the same blind spot that causes it.
get.summary: Outbox depth and age — scrape this

get.description:
Route traffic on this; restart on /health.

Conflating the two restarts a healthy process that is merely waiting on a
dependency.

Only the dependencies a service actually declares are checked. A gateway owns no
tables, so asking it for a database is asking a question whose answer means nothing
— and a readiness probe that reports on something the service does not use is worse
than no probe, because it will eventually fail for a reason nobody can act on.

Reachable only on the compose `back` network (`tests/infra`'s
`test_metrics_never_routed.py` is the lint that keeps it that way) — never behind
Caddy or a gateway, the same rule `ops_monitor`'s own `/metrics` follows.

`db_pool_in_use` is always reported when this service has a database; the three
outbox gauges only when `outbox_model` is configured — same gate as `/health/outbox`,
and the same reason: an app-role connection with no tenant bound sees zero rows.
